day-1.t: Day 1 — The trade and staying safe

v: Understand what a repair technician does
Learn the safety rules before touching a phone

b.v: About 20 minutes. This course teaches the basics; real skill comes from practice on old phones.

v: Most jobs: screen, battery, charging port, software problems, speaker and mic
Harder jobs: board-level faults that need soldering under a microscope
Customers want three things: a fair price, a quick repair and honesty
Lithium batteries can catch fire if bent, pierced or shorted
Never use a metal tool to pry a battery
A swollen battery must be replaced, never pressed back in
Keep a metal tray or sand bucket nearby for a hot battery
Static electricity from your body can kill a chip - use an anti-static mat and wrist strap
Solder and flux give fumes - work with a fan or open window
Protect your eyes when using a heat gun

b.v: Practise on old, dead phones first. Never learn on a customer's phone.
Do this now:|Collect 2 or 3 old phones from family to practise on.|Prepare a clean, well-lit table with a fan.

v: Know the basic toolkit
Start with a small budget
Precision screwdriver set (Phillips, Pentalobe, Tri-point, Torx)
Plastic opening picks and a spudger
Suction cup
Fine tweezers
Anti-static mat and wrist strap
Magnifying lamp
Hot air station or heat gun for softening glue
Soldering iron with fine tips, solder wire and flux
Digital multimeter
Regulated DC power supply
Isopropyl alcohol (99%) and a soft brush for cleaning

b.v: Buy good screwdrivers first; cheap ones strip tiny screws and damage phones. You can add the hot air station and microscope when your work grows.
Do this now:|Make a list of the starter kit with prices from your local market.|Write what you will buy now and what later.

v: Name the main parts
Understand how they connect
Motherboard (logic board) - the brain with processor, memory and chips
Battery - connected to the board with a small connector
Display - glass, touch layer and screen, joined as one part in most phones
Charging port - often on a small sub-board with the mic
Cameras, earpiece, loudspeaker, vibration motor
Flex cables - thin ribbons that join the parts

b.v: Most parts plug into the board with press-fit connectors, like tiny buttons. They come off by lifting gently with a plastic spudger and go back with light finger pressure. Forcing them breaks the pins.

v: Take a photo at every step - it shows where screws and cables go
Screws have different lengths; a long screw in the wrong hole can damage the board
Use a magnetic mat or a paper with marked spots for screws

b.v: Do this now:|Open an old phone and take a photo of the inside.|Label each part on the photo.

v: Open a phone without breaking it
Always disconnect the battery first

b.v: Step by step:|Ask the customer to back up their data.|Note what works and what does not, in front of the customer.|Switch the phone off and remove the SIM tray.

Step by step:|Warm the edges with a heat gun on low for a minute to soften the glue.|Lift a corner with the suction cup.|Slide a plastic pick in and move it slowly around the edge.|Watch for flex cables - many phones open like a book.|Unscrew the shield over the battery connector and disconnect the battery first.

v: Test before you close: power, touch, cameras, sound, charging
Replace the adhesive so the phone stays sealed
Put every screw back in its own hole

b.v: Too much heat can damage the screen or the battery. Keep the heat gun moving and on a low setting.
Do this now:|Open and close an old phone twice.|Time yourself and note what was hard.

v: Fix common software faults
Stay on the right side of the law
Slow or hanging: free up storage, close background apps, update the system
An app crashes: clear its cache, update or reinstall it
Strange behaviour: start in safe mode to see if a downloaded app is the cause
Nothing helps: back up, then factory reset
Stuck on the logo: reinstall the official system software with the maker's tool

b.v: Install system software only from the phone maker. Modified files from unknown websites can carry viruses and steal the customer's data.

v: Never remove an account lock or change the IMEI of a phone - it is illegal and helps thieves
Check that a phone's IMEI is registered with PTA (DIRBS) before you buy or sell a used phone
Unlock only with proof that the customer owns the phone

b.v: Do this now:|On your own phone, check storage, battery use and updates.|Find how to start it in safe mode.

v: Find why a phone won't charge
Replace a battery safely

b.v: Step by step:|Try another cable and adapter.|Look into the port with a light: lint and dust are the most common cause.|Clean it gently with a wooden toothpick or a brush and alcohol - never a metal pin.|Check the charging current with a USB meter.|If still bad, replace the charging port or its sub-board.

v: Drains fast or shuts off at 20%: the battery is old
Swollen: the screen or back lifts - replace at once
Check battery health in settings if the phone shows it

b.v: Step by step:|Disconnect the battery connector first.|Pull the glue tabs slowly, or use a little alcohol under the battery to soften the glue.|Never bend or pierce the battery.|Fit a good-quality battery of the same type and connect it last.
Do this now:|Clean the charging port of an old phone.|Practise removing and refitting its battery.

v: Understand screen types
Replace a screen and test it
LCD - cheaper, has a backlight
OLED / AMOLED - thinner, deeper blacks, more expensive
Original, refurbished and copy parts differ in colour, brightness and touch

b.v: Step by step:|Open the phone and disconnect the battery.|Disconnect the display flex cable.|Move any parts that stay (earpiece, sensors, front camera bracket) to the new screen.|Connect the new screen and battery, and test before closing.|Fit new adhesive and close.
Tell the customer which quality of screen you are fitting and the price of each. A copy screen sold as original ruins your name in the market.
Do this now:|On an old phone, remove and refit the screen.|Write the price difference between two screen qualities in your market.

day-8.t: Day 8 — Speaker, mic, camera and buttons

v: Fix sound and camera faults
Clean before you replace
Test with headphones or a speaker test in settings
Clean the speaker mesh with a soft brush
Check if the phone thinks headphones are plugged in
Replace the speaker if still faulty
Record a voice note to test
Clean the mic hole gently
The main mic is often on the charging sub-board
Blurry photos: clean the lens glass; a cracked lens glass can be replaced
Camera app fails: restart, clear cache, then check the camera connector
Buttons not working: clean, then check the button flex cable

b.v: Do this now:|Test speaker, mic and camera on 2 phones.|Write which part you would check first for each fault.

v: Measure voltage and check continuity
Find a short circuit safely
DC voltage - check battery voltage (a healthy phone battery is about 3.7 to 4.4 V)
Continuity - beeps when two points are connected; checks broken flex cables
Diode mode - compare readings on connector pins with a good board

b.v: If a phone draws high current from the power supply without turning on, there is a short on the board. Technicians find the hot component with a thermal camera or by applying a little alcohol and watching where it dries first. This is advanced work - learn it after the basics.
Always set the meter before touching the probes to the board, and never measure resistance on a powered board.
Do this now:|Measure the voltage of an old phone battery.|Check continuity of a charging cable from end to end.

v: Price fairly and give a warranty
Earn the customer's trust
Customer name and number
Phone model and IMEI
Fault described by the customer and what you saw
Price agreed and delivery date
Customer's signature
Price = part cost + your labour + a small margin
Give a short warranty on your work and parts, in writing
Never charge for a repair you could not do

b.v: Phones hold photos, chats and bank apps. Never open the customer's files, never copy anything, and keep phones locked away at night. Your honesty is your best advertisement.
Take the quiz to get your certificate. Then keep practising on old phones, and consider working with an experienced technician to learn board-level repair.
Do this now:|Design your job card.|Write your price list for 5 common repairs.
